header: Date: 2026-12-10 | Time: 14:00 PST | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Liu (Redwood SE), Rajiv Menon (Lumineer Head of ML), Sara Klein (Lead Data Engineer), Tom Brooks (Security), Alicia Park (Product)
summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on quality evaluation, recent regression results, and fallback/readiness plans. Discussed scoring drift on entity extraction, false positive uptick after prompt compacting, and a proposed 24h throughput test on a Dedicated slot. Security asked for SOC2 excerpts and network diagram. Agreed next steps: tests, updated prompt/scoring artifacts, and scheduling a rollback drill.
topics: Guardrail false positives and redaction rules
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll kick off. quick agenda: quality signals, regressions, test plan, and fallback drill. Ethan is going to run through the numbers.
[00:18] Ethan: hey all, glad to be here. Quick note, I ran the nightly eval — we saw a bump in false positives on entity extraction especially for legal-entity tokens after the prompt compaction we shipped last week. F1 dropped from .87 to .81 on that slice.
[00:36] Rajiv: yeah we flagged that— noticed more 'company name' hallucinations which is a problem for downstream matching. Could be prompt munging or maybe the KV cache config.
[00:51] Sara: to confirm, this only started after you compacted the prompt templates? we changed the template order and removed some clarifying context.
[01:05] Ethan: correct, compacting removed a clarification sentence that seemed redundant, but that line actually anchored the demarcation of legal entities. So tradeoff: token reduction vs prompt clarity.
[01:20] Maya: classic latency vs quality trade. Rajiv, what are your success criteria now — is .85 acceptable or do you need parity with .87?
[01:34] Rajiv: aim is to get back to >= .86 for production guardrail. If we can't we need fallback rules that drop to human-in-loop.
[01:44] Tom: from security side, anything that increases PII/PHI leakage risk is high priority; our retention rules and redaction must be airtight. We need to see the redaction rules and the logs sampling.
[01:58] Maya: we'll share redaction rules and retention SLAs. Sara, can you describe how you're consuming the model outputs?
[02:08] Sara: we run a matching microservice that takes entity outputs and reconciles against the canonical registry; false positives cause bad matches and downstream workflows fail. We do a soft-fail now but in prod that becomes costly.
[02:22] Ethan: one quick datapoint—when we re-ran the eval with the longer clarifier token reintroduced (prompt v1.3) F1 for that slice went to .86. latency increased by ~12ms median.
[02:36] Rajiv: 12ms is acceptable if it gets us back to .86. we prefer correctness.
[02:44] Maya: ok so plan A is revert that clarifier for entity-heavy flows; plan B is add a guardrail that flags low-confidence entities for human verification.
[02:56] Alicia: curious — how will that affect cost? our CFO is sensitive to token costs.
[03:04] Ethan: rough calc — the clarifier adds about 6 tokens per request; at your projected QPS it's a small delta, maybe 3-4% of token spend. The bigger driver is model variant; using the quantized variant reduces token cost but impacts quality slightly.
[03:20] Rajiv: we also discussed dedicated capacity earlier — can Redwood run a 24h sustained test to show stable latency and throughput on the Dedicated slot? we'd like to understand tail latency under sustained load before we commit.
[03:33] Maya: yes we can, Ethan will own. We'll provision a dedicated slot and run a 24h run with your representative workload and share the dashboard.
[03:44] Tom: for the Dedicated test we need network topology and whether the private deployment option changes egress patterns. Also need SOC2/ISO docs.
[03:56] Maya: I'll share the SOC2 excerpts and a simple network diagram, plus notes on VPC peering behavior for Redwood Private.
[04:07] Ethan: quick note on regressions — some of the false positives are correlated with prompt truncation when context windows exceed 1.2k tokens. We saw more hallucinations when the model had to drop the conversation history.
[04:22] Sara: right that's our long-chat flows; we have sessions that are 2-3k tokens. Any ideas?
[04:30] Ethan: options: increase prefix caching to keep the core context, or introduce summary compression to keep essential facts. Redwood Optimize can recommend batching and cache configs — we can run that analysis against your token distribution.
[04:45] Rajiv: summary compression sounds interesting. can you do a demo?
[04:50] Ethan: yes, we can run a small experiment — summarize older turns into a compact bullet list and keep the most recent full context. We've seen it preserve quality and reduce tokens.
[05:02] Maya: ok add that as an experiment to run during the 24h test.
[05:07] Rajiv: switching topics — guardrails. We saw an uptick in benign false positives where the safety filter flags policy text snippets as 'disallowed' because of wording. It interrupts some legitimate workflows.
[05:20] Alicia: that was us — we noticed the safety filter is a bit aggressive on policy citations.
[05:27] Ethan: two levers here: adjust the guardrail thresholds per route, or add route-specific allowlists. We can tune the model-level safety thresholds and add a post-filter that is more context-aware.
[05:40] Sara: route-specific thresholds sound right. We need a way to monitor per-route false positive rate.
[05:47] Maya: the Redwood Console will give per-route metrics once we enable instrumentation; we can push logs to your S3 for audit.
[05:55] Tom: audit logs are required; we also want token-level cost breakdowns and a trace of decisions for compliance.
[06:04] Maya: that's supported — token breakdown and traces per request. we'll map sampling to your retention policy.
[06:12] Rajiv: quick nit — the eval spreadsheet shows our scoring rubric weights: recall 0.4, precision 0.4, contextual fidelity 0.2. we think we need to increase precision weight for this use-case.
[06:24] Ethan: simple change, we'll produce scoring-rubric v2 with precision bumped to 0.55, recall 0.3, fidelity 0.15. We'll run the eval again and share delta.
[06:36] Sara: please also include per-scenario confusion matrices. those helped us root cause last sprint.
[06:43] Ethan: noted.
[06:45] [06:45] Maya: okay let's talk fallback/rollback readiness — we suggested a canary with automatic fallback to a smaller model variant if latency spikes or errors exceed thresholds. Are you comfortable with auto-fallback?
[06:58] Rajiv: yes but only if we have strict thresholds and an alert path to ops. We need a drill to ensure the swap doesn't introduce regressions.
[07:10] Alicia: also ensure the user-facing experience is degraded gracefully — don't surface raw 'model unavailable' errors.
[07:18] Ethan: Redwood supports a layered fallback: model variant, then cached responses, then static human template. We can orchestrate automatic switch with A/B canary and route traffic back after stability.
[07:30] Sara: what about KV cache warmup? if we fallback to a different variant, cold cache will spike latency.
[07:37] Ethan: true — we recommend a rolling warmup where we pre-warm KV cache for the fallback model with typical prefixes during the canary. The Dedicated test can emulate warmup scenarios.
[07:48] Rajiv: timeline: we want the rollback drill next Tuesday the 16th, and we'd like Redwood to coordinate so our ops team can participate.
[07:57] Maya: we'll set that — add to next steps.
[08:02] Tom: security check — if we run Dedicated in your cloud, what encryption-at-rest keys are used? KMS? HSM?
[08:10] Maya: Redwood Private integrates with customer KMS, and for Hosted we use provider-managed KMS with customer-managed key options on Dedicated/Private. We'll include details in the doc.
[08:22] Tom: also need proof that logs can be forwarded to our SIEM without exposing keys.
[08:27] Ethan: logs can be forwarded over TLS and we can obfuscate token text per your retention rules.
[08:34] Sara: small thing—we're seeing intermittent 95th p99 tails around 420ms during load spikes. what's the expected SLA for Dedicated?
[08:44] Maya: Dedicated target p99 is 350ms for your config, but we'll put in the SLA details in the contract draft. The 24h run will show us how close we get.
[08:55] Rajiv: if p99 can't be met, we'll need an operational playbook.
[09:00] Maya: agreed — we'll prepare a playbook (throttle, fallback, ops alerting) and share with you.
[09:06] Ethan: returning to quality — we tested prompt v2 which reintroduced clarifier plus a compact summary step. Early numbers: entity F1 back to .865, latency +18ms median vs v1. So it's a middle ground.
[09:21] Rajiv: that looks promising. what about cost delta?
[09:24] Ethan: about 6.8% token increase compared to compacted v1, but still ~2% less than full verbose v0 baseline.
[09:34] Alicia: finance wants a concrete cost/quality curve to justify changes. can we get that in a one-page chart?
[09:40] Maya: yes we'll produce a cost vs quality slide and share it with Alicia and Rajiv.
[09:46] Sara: any blockers on our side? we need to confirm retention SLAs and provide sample data for the 24h test.
[09:55] Rajiv: we'll sanitize sample logs and produce a representative QPS pattern by tomorrow.
[10:00] Maya: perfect — so recap of technical outcomes: revert clarifier for entity routes OR use prompt v2 (clarifier + summary) as experiment; run 24h Dedicated throughput + warmup tests; produce scoring rubric v2 and confusion matrices; prepare rollback drill; share security docs.
[10:16] Ethan: I'll kick off the 24h run as soon as we get the sample workload and configure instrumentation to collect p50/p95/p99, token costs, and per-route FP rates.
[10:28] Tom: please ensure logs sent to our S3 are redacted per rules, and include a sampling policy.
[10:36] Maya: will do. I'll email the SOC2/ISO excerpts and network diagram after this call.
[10:42] Rajiv: timeline check — 24h run results by 12/12, scoring rubric by 12/11, rollback drill 12/16. Is that feasible?
[10:52] Maya: yes those dates are aligned.
[10:55] Alicia: last question — any competitors we should be worried about in procurement? we've had outreach from Inferia and CloudAI but their latency / observability picture wasn't great.
[11:06] Maya: noted, we'll include a short comparison in the follow-up doc focusing on observability, guardrails, and cost controls.
[11:14] Rajiv: ok thanks everyone.
[11:17] Maya: quick recap of owners and we'll close.
[11:20] Ethan: (murmur) thanks all.
[11:23] [End 45:00]
